pd_dollhouse_2.summary: Nora tells the children to keep the stranger secret and sends them away.
Alone and agitated, Nora busies herself with sewing and the tree.
Helmer returns and Nora denies anyone visited.
Helmer saw Krogstad leave and catches Nora in her lie.
Helmer scolds his songbird indulgently, then settles comfortably by the stove.

pd_dollhouse_3.summary: Helmer reassures Nora her fears are fancy and goes to his office.
Alone, Nora panics, fearing what Helmer will do, desperate for escape.
Rank arrives and hints that something is about to happen soon.
Rank reveals he is dying and will bar Helmer from his sickroom.
Nora deflects with light talk of his father's rich indulgences.

pd_dollhouse_4.summary: Mrs Linde plans to retrieve Krogstad's letter and tells Nora to stall Helmer.
Nora begs Helmer to devote the evening to helping her rehearse.
Helmer heads for the letterbox; Nora frantically begs him not to.
Nora plays the Tarantella to distract Helmer, and he sits to play.
Nora dances wildly while Helmer plays and Rank watches.

pd_dollhouse_5.summary: Rank knocks late and Helmer reluctantly lets him in.
Rank and Helmer banter about champagne and the merry evening.
Nora probes; Rank confirms his examination yielded certainty of death.
They discuss costumes for the next ball as Rank hints at his choice.

pd_dollhouse_6.summary: Helmer begs Nora to stay as she gathers her cloak and bag.
Nora frees Helmer from obligation and they exchange rings.
Nora refuses letters or help; only a miraculous change could reunite them.
Nora leaves; Helmer collapses, hopes briefly, and the door slams below.

pd_earnest_0.summary: Algernon banters with Lane about piano playing and cucumber sandwiches.
Algernon questions Lane about drunk champagne; Lane wryly defends himself.
Lane announces Ernest Worthing, who arrives teasing Algy about eating.
Algernon probes Jack's country life; Jack fumbles about Shropshire and the tea.

pd_earnest_1.summary: Jack and Gwendolen profess love; she adores the name Ernest.
Jack tries to sell her on the name Jack; Gwendolen scorns it.
Jack proposes clumsily on his knees and Gwendolen accepts.
Lady Bracknell enters, forbids the engagement, and sends Gwendolen to the carriage.

pd_earnest_2.summary: Cecily avoids German lessons and wonders about Uncle Jack's wicked brother.
Cecily and Miss Prism spar over diaries, memory and three-volume novels.
Dr. Chasuble arrives; Cecily slyly suggests Miss Prism walk with him.
Miss Prism discovers a headache and leaves strolling with Chasuble.

pd_earnest_3.summary: Chasuble, Prism and Cecily leave the brothers to their reconciliation.
Jack orders Algy to leave; Merriman reveals Algernon's luggage unpacked.
Jack orders the dog-cart, and Algernon calls him a liar.
They trade insults about clothes and vanity until Jack storms off.
Algernon, in love, finds Cecily and they lament their parting.

pd_earnest_4.summary: Cecily and Gwendolen trade barbs over the engagement to Ernest.
With servants present, they exchange icily polite insults about country and town.
Cecily serves sugar and cake against Gwendolen's explicit wishes.
Gwendolen warns Cecily she may go too far; open hostility erupts.
Jack enters and Gwendolen greets him rapturously as her Ernest.

pd_earnest_5.summary: The men vow to be christened; couples fall into each other's arms.
Lady Bracknell arrives and forbids all contact between Gwendolen and Jack.
Algernon flusteredly explains that Bunbury has died, quite exploded.
Algernon announces his engagement to Cecily, startling Lady Bracknell.
Lady Bracknell interrogates Cecily's origins; Jack coldly lists her addresses.

pd_earnest_6.summary: Jack introduces Algernon as his brother and they shake hands.
Gwendolen demands his name; Jack quizzes Lady Bracknell about his christening.
Jack tears through the Army Lists searching for his father's name.
Jack discovers his name truly is Ernest; Gwendolen forgives him.
Three couples embrace; Jack declares the importance of being earnest.

pd_sisters_0.summary: Olga recalls their father's death a year ago on Irina's name-day.
Olga remembers Moscow in spring; the sisters long to return there.
Irina feels joyful; Olga confides she wishes she were married.
Tuzenbach announces Vershinin's visit and gossips about his troubled wife.
Soleni and Chebutikin wander in muttering absurd remarks.

pd_sisters_1.summary: Andrey dismisses a visitor and retreats to his room.
Masha confides her disillusioned marriage and disdain for civilians.
Vershinin laments Russian discontent and his miserable marriage to Masha.
Vershinin kisses her hand and declares his love; Masha, afraid, yields.
Irina and Tuzenbach enter as he pledges to walk her home forever.
